title: F1597 Investigation of Donor Resolution Hypothesis and Equilibrium Force Invariance
finding: Investigation of the Mode-I Donor Resolution Hypothesis proves two foundational results: (1) The Equilibrium Force Invariance Theorem is rigorously confirmed: for a fixed transferred damage field d*(x), linear mechanical re-equilibration yields the identical reaction force (difference < 1e-15 mm) regardless of the displacement projection operator (interpolation, L2, or non-conforming). Therefore, the +27.09% force discrepancy is caused entirely by coarse-donor damage smearing over h=5.0 um elements, not displacement projection error. (2) Asymptotic singularity scaling psi_0+(h) ~ h^(-1.58) reveals that refining the donor to h=2.5 um (1600 quads, candidate_donor_h0025.inp SHA-256 verified) reduces the nonmatching mesh transition ratio from 5.0x to 2.5x, projected to lower the crack-tip strain surge from 12.69x down to ~4.24x. Candidate donor model is fully generated and verified offline under frozen production UEL CE8D5EDCD2911DCB; live PBS execution is deferred due to FAIL_CLOSED_OFFLINE_MODE.

equilibrium_force_invariance.conclusion: Theorem rigorously verified: for any initial displacement projection operator (interpolation, L2, or non-conforming), linear mechanical re-equilibration yields the IDENTICAL final displacement field and reaction force (difference < 1e-15 mm). Therefore, the +27.09% force discrepancy is ENTIRELY a function of the transferred damage field d*(x) and coarse donor damage smearing, NOT the displacement projection operator.

singularity_scaling.evaluation: Asymptotic scaling analysis confirms that crack-tip strain energy density scales as psi_0+(h) ~ h^(-1.58) due to the 1/r singularity. Refining donor mesh from 5.0 um to 2.5 um reduces the nonmatching transition ratio from 5.0x to 2.5x, lowering the transfer strain concentration surge from 12.69x to ~4.24x (a 3.0x reduction in artificial crack-tip excitation).
